;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]], [[2019 Western Libya offensive]]
**Forces loyal to the [[Government of National Accord]] retake [[Tripoli International Airport]] from the [[Libyan National Army]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/libyan-govt-forces-retake-tripoli-airport-from-haftar/1445449 (Anadolu Agency)]
**One of the vice chairmen of the GNA [[Presidential Council (Libya)|Presidential Council]], [[Ali Faraj Qatrani]], defects to the [[House of Representatives (Libya)|Tobruk-based government]]. [https://aawsat.com/english/home/article/1669676/sarraj-deputy-quits-voices-support-libyan-national-army (Asharq Al-Awsat)]
**A warplane loyal to [[Field marshal (Libya)|Field Marshal]] [[Khalifa Haftar]], reported to be a [[Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23|MiG-23]], strikes [[Mitiga International Airport]], the only functional airport in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]]. A LNA spokesman says civilian planes were not targeted in the air raid. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/apr/08/eu-uk-urges-france-to-condemn-khalifa-haftar-assault-on-tripoli (''The Guardian'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**A roadside bomb kills three [[United States|U.S.]] troops and one civilian contractor near [[Bagram Airfield]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-47860816 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*''[[The Nation]]''{{'s}} editor [[Katrina vanden Heuvel]] announces that she will step down as editor after 24 years, on June 15, 2019. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/08/business/media/katrina-vanden-heuvel-the-nation.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Law and crime
*Nationwide protests against animal cruelty take place in [[Australia]]. In the city of [[Melbourne]], protesters blocked a major intersection for four hours before it was dispatched by police; several people were arrested. [https://www.news.com.au/lifestyle/food/animal-activists-hold-protests-around-the-country-on-one-year-anniversary-of-confronting-documentary/news-story/4bce0ca02fa6c71f000638f5bf0379c9 (News.com.au)]
*The [[Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport]] in the United Kingdom releases a white paper proposing to set up an independent regulatory body which would require Internet companies to [[Internet censorship in the United Kingdom|remove content and block websites]] considered harmful. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-47826946 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 college admissions bribery scandal]]
**American actress [[Felicity Huffman]] and 13 other defendants involved in a conspiracy regarding admission to prestigious colleges have agreed to plead guilty in the matter, prosecutors say. The 14 individuals are among 50 people accused of engaging in schemes that involved cheating on college entrance exams and paying $25 million in bribes to secure their children admission to well-known colleges. [https://wkzo.com/news/articles/2019/apr/08/felicity-huffman-others-to-plead-guilty-in-us-college-admissions-scandal-prosecutors/ (WKZO)]
*U.S. district judge [[Richard Seeborg]] halts the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]’s policy of sending some asylum seekers to [[Mexico]] while their cases are pending in the United States. The national injunction will take effect Friday. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-immigration-asylum/u-s-judge-halts-trump-policy-of-returning-asylum-seekers-to-mexico-idUSKCN1RK2E6 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**[[Eric Swalwell 2020 presidential campaign]]
***[[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Eric Swalwell]] from [[California]] announces he is running for the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party's]] nomination to be [[President of the United States]] in the 2020 presidential election. [https://www.foxnews.com/politics/rep-eric-swalwell-announces-2020-run-on-colberts-late-show (Fox News)]
*[[List of Trump administration dismissals and resignations|Trump administration dismissals and resignations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] terminates the employment of [[Randolph Alles]], the [[Director of the United States Secret Service|Director]] of the [[United States Secret Service]]. [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2019/04/08/politics/randolph-tex-alles-secret-service-director/index.html (CNN)]
*[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces the designation of the entirety of [[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] as a [[Foreign Terrorist Organization]] (FTO), effective April 15. This will be the first time the [[United States]] has designated a part of another government as a terrorist organization. [https://www.state.gov/secretary/remarks/2019/04/290966.htm (United States Department of State)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-designates-irans-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps-as-a-terrorist-organization/ (CBS News)]

;Science and technology
*[[David Saint-Jacques]] becomes the fourth Canadian astronaut to take part in a [[spacewalk]] and the first in 12 years as he begins a roughly seven-hour mission. [https://www.thespec.com/news-story/9272303-astronaut-david-saint-jacques-first-canadian-to-perform-spacewalk-in-12-years/ (''The Hamilton Spectator'')] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/david-saint-jacques-first-spacewalk-1.5088545 (CBC.ca)]
*[[List of gravitational wave observations|Gravitational wave observations]]
**[[LIGO]] and [[Virgo interferometer|Virgo]] detect a gravitational wave from a galaxy 6 billion light-years away in the direction of [[Cassiopeia (constellation)|Cassiopeia]], with further details being released on April 10. [https://www.newscientist.com/article/2199107-ligo-has-spotted-another-gravitational-wave-just-after-turning-back-on/ (''New Scientist'')]

;Sports
*[[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia Cavaliers]] defeat the [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech Red Raiders]], [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|85–77]] in [[overtime (sports)|overtime]], to win their first national title. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/04/08/virginia-vs-texas-tech/ (''The Washington Post'')]
